name: Fast deployment: slim installer for trial users
description:
## Goal
Make codx-junior cheap to build/pull and one command to run, so people can test it in minutes.

## Analysis (done)
Full analysis written to `codx-junior-installer/FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`. Key findings:
- Python deps include `vllm`, `torch`, `sentence-transformers`, `playwright` that the code either never imports (`torch`), imports lazily with graceful fallback (`sentence_transformers`) or marks DEPRECATED (`vllm_cpu_ai.py`).
- Base image installs `texlive*`, `firefox-esr`, `tesseract-ocr`, `pandoc`, `fuse*` for on-demand features.
- Client is built inside the runtime image (`nvm install`, `npm i`, `npm run build-only`) and served with `npm run preview` (node + node_modules in production).
- `run_api.sh` runs `sudo chown -R $HOME` and `uv sync` on every start, and can run `install_api.sh` (torch/vllm install) inside a cold container. `api/uv.lock` exists but is unused.
- No root `.dockerignore` although the build context is the repo root.
- 8 services in the default compose (2 one-shot init containers, traefik, localai, client, 2 API processes).

## Scope of this card (implementation)
1. Root `.dockerignore`.
2. `api/pyproject.toml`: move torch/sentence-transformers/playwright to optional extras, drop vllm from base.
3. Slim base image (`python:3.11-slim`), build with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, no texlive/firefox.
4. Multi-stage client build (static output served by nginx or FastAPI StaticFiles).
5. `run_api.sh` / `run_client.sh`: no installs and no recursive chown at runtime.
6. Compose: delete init containers, profiles for traefik / localai / milvus / workspaces, remove dev bind mount, run background worker via `supervisor.conf` in the API container.
7. Installer script: preflight checks, pull-by-default, `--build`, idempotent, prints the URL.

## Acceptance
- `docker run … codxjunior/codx-junior:latest` serves the UI on :19981 without cloning the repo.
- Image ≤ ~1.2 GB; no torch/vllm/TeX/Node inside; restart does no installs.
- Plain `docker compose up` starts only what is needed to see the UI; extras are opt-in profiles.
- `docs/getting-started.md` documents the trial path first.
